subject: Assessing vertical privacy addendum and operational constraints for Keystone pilot
messages:
From: Tara Miller <tara.miller@keystonehealth.org>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: it-ops@keystonehealth.org
Date: 2026-11-01T08:14:00Z
Subject: Pilot: vertical privacy addendum questions (HIPAA + GLBA overlap)

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team asked me to surface a concise list of asks so we can determine whether we can onboard Redwood for a 3-month pilot across our provider network. Topline items are:

- Can Redwood sign a combined HIPAA BAA + GLBA addendum, or do you propose separate instruments?
- We need a full list of subprocessors with geographic residency for the pilot (US only requirement).
- For key management: can we provide customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for PHI at-rest encryption? If not, what compensating controls?
- Audit logs: retention for 12 months and access method (API vs syslog).
- Data residency: we want guaranteed US-only processing and at-rest storage for pilot data.

Attached is a short questionnaire from our counsel to expedite scoping (Keystone_privacy_questions.pdf). Please let me know who on your side is point for legal and infra so we can set a 30-min follow-up early next week.

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Miller | Senior Counsel, Keystone Health

Subject: Re: Pilot: vertical privacy addendum questions (HIPAA + GLBA overlap)

Tara — thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. Looping in our Legal (Irene), Product/Platform (Laura) and Sales Ops (Aditya) to map technical & contractual constraints.

Quick answers up-front:
- We typically offer a single DPA with addenda-style sections for HIPAA/GLBA obligations; we can draft a combined instrument for review.
- Subprocessor inventory and residency are provided; we'll surface the minimal set used for the pilot.
- Customer-managed KMS support depends on deployment mode: Hosted API (shared KMS, limited CMEK) vs Dedicated/Private (CMEK/HSM available).

Irene, Laura — can you confirm (1) whether we can commit to US-only subprocessors for the pilot, (2) CMEK availability on Dedicated vs Hosted, and (3) typical audit log retention and export formats?

Tara — propose a 30-min call Monday (Nov 2) 10:00-10:30 PT or Nov 3 09:00-09:30 PT. Mateo

--

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai, tara.miller@keystonehealth.org

Date: 2026-11-02T09:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot: vertical privacy addendum questions (HIPAA + GLBA overlap)

Hi all — I reviewed Tara's questionnaire and sketched a pragmatic path for the pilot. Attaching a redline starter (draft_addendum_redwood_v1.docx) and our subprocessor inventory snapshot (subprocessor_inventory_20261102.csv). Key points below.

1) Single addendum approach: We can produce one instrument with discrete sections for BAA obligations (HIPAA) and GLBA requirements. That keeps signature/negotiation simpler for the pilot.

2) Subprocessors & residency: For Hosted API customers, some infra subs (CDN, monitoring, analytics) may be multi-region. For a US-only processing guarantee we should route Keystone to Redwood Dedicated or Private for the pilot; otherwise we can offer contractual assurances plus technical constraints but not a hard residency SLA.

3) CMEK / HSM: Customer-managed key support is available in Redwood Dedicated and Private. Hosted API customers do not currently have full CMEK control for tokenization of model state; we can offer envelope encryption and a Bring-Your-Own-Key option in Dedicated.

4) Audit logs: We retain request/response metadata for 12 months by default for enterprise accounts. Logs are accessible via API export or SFTP delivery; we can also stream to a customer syslog/tenant log endpoint for the pilot. More detailed request-payload logging is redaction-enabled by policy.

5) Operational constraints and timelines: If Keystone requires US-only subprocessors and CMEK, the quickest viable path is a Dedicated pilot (provisioning ~4–6 weeks) versus Private (on-prem) which is longer. If Keystone is flexible on CMEK initially, we can sequence: Hosted pilot (2 weeks) with limited dataset, then Dedicated cutover.

I'll be happy to walk through the draft addendum on the call.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: draft_addendum_redwood_v1.docx (excerpted clauses), subprocessor_inventory_20261102.csv
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-02T14:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot: vertical privacy addendum questions (HIPAA + GLBA overlap)

Tara — adding technical detail from platform side and attaching a network/processing diagram (redwood_network_diagram_v2.pdf). Short summary:

- Residency: For Dedicated we can pin GPUs, storage, and control plane routing to a single US region; storage encryption at-rest uses AES-256 and integrates with customer KMS in Dedicated via CMEK hooks.
- CMEK scope: CMEK protects object storage at-rest; model runtime ephemeral state (KV cache) currently does not persist to customer KMS in Hosted mode. We are working on runtime KMS bindings but cannot commit for Hosted customers for the pilot.
- Subprocessor minimization: We can strip analytics/usage telemetry for the pilot to reduce subprocessors. The inventory Irene attached shows which suppliers would remain.

Operational ask: If Keystone wants Dedicated with CMEK and US-only subprocessors, we'll need an internal SRE-run provisioning ticket (approx 3 business days to schedule) and a short security onboarding call to exchange certificates and KMS ARNs.

Proposed call agenda (30 min):
1) Legal redline walkthrough (Irene) — 10 min
2) Technical constraints and provisioning plan (Laura) — 10 min
3) Timeline & next steps (Mateo/Aditya) — 10 min

Thanks — attaching redwood_network_diagram_v2.pdf.

Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
